claims.text: R41/R8: an inter-account transfer that neither the rule table nor the profile names (main FPS TO 12345678 -100.00 on 01-06, savings FPS FROM 87654321 100.00 on 01-07) is paired before compute_case merges the accounts. Both lines become own_account_transfer with rule pairing:<account>:<id>. The credit leaves unexplained money in (M25) and moves to M19. It also leaves M2, M16, M26 and, with its debit, M9. Each account's own figures carry the pairing too, and the paired lines are not in the judgement queue.

R9: when a debit has two equal candidate credits in other accounts within the days, it is not paired. Both credits stay unexplained (M25), M19 is 0, and the workspace judgement queue lists the debit and both candidates as possible_own_account_transfer, each naming the others in pairs_with by case id.

A per-line override outranks a pairing. Overriding the paired credit unpairs its debit, and the other account's figures that moved are marked as resting on an override (R17). A credit outside the days does not pair.
Every test in tests/test_multi_account.py passes, the earlier 21 included.
The full suite, the marker tiers, the offline evals, ruff and compileall all pass.

dispositions.finding: major (src/cma/metrics.py:468, R41): compute_case computes combined flows with no own-account pairing; R8 is implemented nowhere, so an unnamed inter-account transfer is counted on both sides of the combined figures (main:M1 -100 / savings:S1 +100 with no own_accounts in the profile).
dispositions.evidence: Per the owner's guidance, pairing is now built in the case pipeline. categorise.pair_own_accounts (R8, R9) pairs a debit in one account with the single same-amount credit in another account within PAIRING_DAYS (3). Lines an override or a protected verdict settled are skipped. A debit with more than one candidate, or a credit that more than one debit could take, is left unpaired and returned as a group. overrides.case_figures now categorises every account first, pairs across them (and across the no-override copies when any override is applied, so marking stays right), and only then computes each account's figures. compute_case then merges the paired statements. M9 treats a paired line as own money, as it does a profile own account (R6). The groups reach the workspace queue and the pack's queue as possible_own_account_transfer. Proven by test_p11_unnamed_transfer_between_accounts_is_paired_and_left_out_of_combined_flows (the reviewer's repro shape: the credit is in M19, not M25) and test_p11_two_equal_candidates_leave_the_debit_unpaired_and_listed.

notes: The pairing window has no configuration key yet. 'The configured number of days' is categorise.PAIRING_DAYS = 3, a module constant, because adding a key to the thresholds or firm file would change a shared contract the design does not list. T34 can make it configurable. A paired line records the rule 'pairing:<account>:<line id>', naming its other half; the module docstring lists the new provenance form. Pairing never runs for a one-account case, so the single-account figures, P7 and the dual run do not move. T34 keeps its own tests and edge cases on top: a credit more than one debit could take, a pair against a profile-named line, and synthetic two-account truth through the pairing.
